newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch see deal on UK borders in new EU treaty.
newsitem.headline: Dutch see deal on UK borders in new EU treaty.

text.p: The Dutch European Union presidency predicted on Wednesday that Britain would secure legal guarantees in the current EU treaty review that it can retain control over its borders.
But it said any move to let Britain do this would be part of a wider package with its EU partners.
"I imagine that the end result will be that there will be legal language...but it's part of a bigger package," Dutch European Affairs Minister Michiel Patijn told a news conference.

"There are no unilateral giveaways in this department," he said, after EU member states' permanent representatives met for three days to fine tune the new EU treaty, due to be concluded at the EU's Amsterdam summit on June 16-17.

He was speaking after Britain's new Home Secretary Jack Straw reaffirmed on Monday after his first meeting with his EU partners that the new British Labour government was determined to maintain national control over its border, asylum and immigration policies.
Britain's continental partners want an agreement to drop internal EU border controls.

Straw said that while it made sense for a central European country like Germany to dispense with border controls, it did not for the British Isles and that in the EU treaty review Britain was demanding cast iron guarantees it could keep its controls.

Although the new Labour government has discarded many Conservative-era standpoints seen as nationalist and anti-European, it shares the unwillingness of its predecessor to give up sovereignty over borders and immigration policy.
Patijn said that the Dutch presidency would be drawing up a new treaty text, aiming at settling outstanding issues, but that it was not clear how this would be presented.
Some of the more difficult issues would inevitably have to be resolved by EU leaders meeting in Amsterdam, he said.
